Why accountability keeps breaking

I have watched more OKR rollouts die in month two than I can count. The goals get written, everyone nods, and nobody opens the document again until December.

It is almost never a discipline problem. Look closely and you find the same three failures. The goal was written so loosely that two people can both assume the other one owns it. The manager kept the interesting work because explaining it would have taken forty minutes. And nothing was checked between the kickoff and the review, so the review turned into an argument about who remembers what.

I hit all three while building the people function at Preply as it scaled, and again at Wargaming. None of them got fixed by asking people to try harder.

What you get instead

A system where ownership is obvious and progress is visible without anyone chasing it. Goals set with OKR so that one name sits against each result. Indicators that come from your actual success factors rather than a template someone downloaded. Work that moves down through six levels of delegation instead of piling up on your desk. RACI so responsibility never falls into the gap between two roles. And a performance review that produces a decision, because everything it needs was already discussed in March.

Who is teaching this

Mike, the number one HR instructor on Udemy. More than 1.6 million course enrolments, over 150,000 professionals trained, PHRi and SHRM-CP certified, HRCI representative in more than 10 countries. I built the people function of the unicorn Preply and worked at Wargaming, Alfa-Bank and iDeals. Everything in this course is what I actually used, including the parts that failed first.

How the course runs

We start with goals, because nothing downstream works if the objective is vague. OKR from first principles: the planning cycle, the launch, running the quarter, closing it properly, then case studies from Google, Intel, MyFitnessPal, Preply and iDeals. Then measurement — how to derive indicators from critical success factors, how to design them so behaviour actually shifts, and the six myths that quietly ruin most KPI systems.

After that, delegation. The psychological barriers first, since that is the real blocker, then SMART and the Eisenhower matrix for choosing what to hand over, RACI for assigning it, and GROW for using delegation to develop someone rather than just offload work.

The last part is the machinery that keeps it alive between reviews: one-on-ones that surface a problem while it is still a correction, feedback that changes behaviour, and the full performance management cycle through to the decisions on pay, promotion, development or exit.

- Practical assignments and real business cases

- A section with additional courses, tools and resources

A word before you start

Accountability is not a value you put on a wall. It is a set of mechanics, and you can install them in a quarter. The managers who get handed bigger things are simply the ones whose commitments reliably land. Enrol now and start the first lesson today.

Why delivery is not the same as change

The methodology argument gets most of the attention — predictive against adaptive, Gantt against sprint — and it is the least interesting part of the problem. A plan can be correct and still fail, because the process underneath was never described, so the new way has nothing to replace. Or because the people affected were informed rather than involved, and informed people comply until you stop watching. Or because you had responsibility for the outcome and authority over nobody, and nobody told you that is the normal condition of the job.

Thirty-six lessons in four parts. Ce cours t’invite à travailler sur quatre dimensions essentielles : ta motivation, ton équilibre émotionnel, les challenges qui te stimulent et la manière dont tu construis tes journées.

L’objectif est simple : apprendre à mieux réagir aux moments difficiles et créer davantage de place pour les activités, les projets et les expériences qui te font réellement vibrer.

Rééquilibre tes journées

Une mauvaise journée au travail, une contrariété ou un moment stressant peut rapidement déborder sur tout le reste de ta journée.

Tu découvriras le principe du rééquilibrage émotionnel par l’activité : après une période difficile, créer volontairement un moment positif qui te permet de changer de dynamique.

Restaurant, cinéma, massage, promenade, sport, activité créative, moment avec tes proches… tu apprendras à identifier les activités qui fonctionnent pour toi et à leur faire une vraie place dans ton quotidien.

L’objectif n’est pas de nier les émotions difficiles, mais de ne pas leur laisser automatiquement toute la journée.

Challenge-toi pour retrouver ta motivation

Nous avons parfois besoin d’un défi pour nous sentir pleinement engagés.

Tu apprendras à identifier et à créer des challenges intrinsèques : des défis que tu choisis parce qu’ils te stimulent personnellement, te donnent envie de progresser et apportent davantage d’intensité à ce que tu fais.

Tu réfléchiras également à ta mission de vie : non pas comme une réponse magique que tu dois absolument trouver, mais comme une direction qui peut t’aider à comprendre ce qui compte réellement pour toi et ce qui te donne envie d’avancer.

Utilise des déclencheurs de motivation

Parfois, une vidéo, un livre, une musique, une histoire ou une phrase suffit à provoquer un déclic.

Tu vas apprendre à identifier les contenus qui te stimulent réellement et à les utiliser consciemment lorsque tu as besoin de retrouver de l’élan.

Ces déclencheurs peuvent t’aider à sortir d’une période de passivité et à te poser une question essentielle :

« Qu’est-ce que je suis en train de faire, et qu’est-ce que j’ai réellement envie de faire maintenant ? »

L’objectif n’est pas de dépendre constamment d’une motivation extérieure, mais de savoir utiliser intelligemment ce qui peut réveiller ta propre envie d’agir.

Crée ta journée parfaite

À quoi ressemble une journée qui te fait vraiment plaisir ?

Dans cette partie, tu vas imaginer et construire ta journée parfaite en fonction de tes valeurs, de ton rythme, de tes priorités et de ce qui te procure réellement de l’énergie.

Travail, projets personnels, plaisir, repos, relations, challenges : tu vas réfléchir à la place que tu souhaites donner à chacun.

Ta journée parfaite n’est pas un planning rigide à reproduire exactement tous les jours. C’est plutôt une boussole qui t’aide à comprendre ce que tu aimerais retrouver plus souvent dans ta vie.

Prends du recul sur les pensées négatives

Certaines pensées méritent notre attention. D’autres tournent simplement en boucle et consomment notre énergie.

Tu apprendras à mieux les observer, à prendre de la distance et à éviter qu’une contrariété momentanée occupe tout ton espace mental.

Il ne s’agit pas de devenir positif en permanence. Une émotion difficile ou une pensée négative fait partie de la vie. L’objectif est plutôt de développer des moyens de retrouver progressivement ton équilibre et ton envie d’avancer.

  • Créer progressivement un quotidien plus proche de tes priorités.

Ce cours s’adresse à ceux qui souhaitent retrouver davantage de motivation, mieux traverser les journées difficiles et construire un quotidien plus stimulant et plus épanouissant.

Tu ne peux pas contrôler tout ce qui arrive dans une journée. Mais tu peux agir sur les challenges que tu choisis, les activités auxquelles tu accordes de la place et la manière dont tu retrouves ton équilibre après un moment difficile.

A pitch deck is a concise and visually engaging presentation that is typically used in business settings to convey a company's or project's key information, value proposition, and investment opportunity. Pitch decks are primarily used when seeking investments, partnerships, or to secure new clients. They serve as a persuasive tool to convey the essence of your business or idea quickly and effectively. A well-crafted pitch deck can make a significant difference in the success of a business, startup, or project.

Here are the key components and the needs of usage for a pitch deck in a business context:

  1. Introduction: Start with a compelling introduction that grabs the audience's attention and provides an overview of your business or project.

  2. Problem Statement: Clearly define the problem or need that your product or service addresses. This sets the stage for why your business is relevant.

  3. Solution: Present your solution and how it addresses the identified problem. Explain how your product or service works and what makes it unique.

  4. Market Opportunity: Describe the market size and potential for your business. This includes the target audience and its demographics.

  5. Business Model: Explain how your business will generate revenue, your pricing strategy, and the sales channels you plan to use.

  6. Traction: Showcase any significant achievements, customer testimonials, or partnerships to build credibility.

  7. Competitive Analysis: Identify your competitors and explain how your business is positioned relative to them. Highlight your competitive advantages.

  8. Team: Introduce your team and their relevant experience. This builds trust and confidence in your ability to execute the business plan.

  9. Financial Projections: Present your financial forecasts, including revenue, expenses, and profitability projections. This demonstrates the potential for a return on investment.

  10. Ask: Clearly state what you are seeking from your audience, whether it's investment, partnership, or something else.


The skills related to pitching, business presenting, and business communication are important for experts and companies for several reasons:

  1. Securing Funding: Effective pitching skills are crucial when seeking investments or funding. A well-presented pitch deck can significantly increase the chances of attracting investors.

  2. Building Credibility: Strong presentation skills can help a company or individual build credibility with clients, partners, and stakeholders. A professional presentation conveys competence and confidence.

  3. Effective Communication: Business communication skills are essential for conveying ideas, plans, and strategies within a company. Clear and persuasive communication can drive team alignment and enhance productivity.

  4. Client Acquisition: In sales and client-facing roles, effective presentation and communication skills can help in acquiring new clients or customers. It can make the difference between a successful pitch and a missed opportunity.

  5. Career Advancement: For individuals, mastering these skills can lead to career advancement. Professionals who can effectively communicate their ideas and lead presentations tend to stand out and progress in their careers.

  6. Team Collaboration: Effective communication and presentation skills are essential for collaboration within teams. They help in conveying objectives, sharing updates, and ensuring everyone is on the same page.


Strong understanding of pitching, business presenting skills, and business communication skills is crucial in today's competitive business environment. These skills not only enable companies to attract investments, win clients, and build credibility but also support the career growth of individuals. A combination of these skills can lead to more successful and impactful business endeavors.
